technical_and_design_decisions: Extend the existing binding abstraction so multiple endpoint instances can coexist for the same binding type, with explicit source and destination connection configuration and backward-compatible behavior for existing single-system configurations.
Resolve HDFS high-availability namenodes through the configured Hadoop HA nameservice and Hadoop client APIs rather than constructing a non-HA proxy directly.
Move the Cassandra and analytic-PMML modules into the target s-c-s repository with minimal functional changes, preserving their existing module contracts and configuration conventions.
Expose job composition through version-compatible REST endpoints returning a composition flag and a graph-oriented JSON representation of parent-child relationships.
Reuse the existing web application's routing, styling, and data-fetching patterns for job visualization and navigation rather than introducing a new frontend framework.
Represent composed jobs as graph nodes and relationships, while retaining standalone jobs as a single identifiable entity.
Maintain backward compatibility for existing REST consumers and UI behavior wherever the specification does not require a breaking change.
Use automated unit, integration, API, module, and UI-level regression tests for the increment, supplemented by manual end-to-end verification.
assumptions: The work is performed by one developer familiar with Java, Spring, Hadoop, Cassandra, PMML, REST, and the existing Spring XD or s-c-s codebases.
Existing repositories, build scripts, CI infrastructure, test frameworks, and deployment environments are available and operational.
The specification describes an enhancement to an existing product; no greenfield platform, authentication system, or infrastructure provisioning is required.
The existing UI already contains job list and job detail pages, routing, and reusable visualization components that can be extended.
The existing job model contains sufficient parent-child or composition metadata; only mapping, persistence access, API exposure, and presentation changes are needed.
Cassandra and analytic-PMML modules already exist in the source system and can be ported without redesigning their runtime behavior or adding major new features.

HDFS HA configuration follows standard Hadoop nameservice and namenode configuration conventions, and compatibility with every Hadoop distribution is not required beyond the supported project versions.
No external-system credentials, schemas, or production data migrations need to be created as part of this increment.

Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation updates, and developer-level integration verification, but excludes elapsed waiting time and production rollout.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing binding model, HDFS module-location code, source and target module repositories, job APIs, persistence model, frontend routes, build configuration, and current tests. Produce an implementation map and identify compatibility constraints.

activities.activity_name: Multiple external systems for one binding type
activities.activity_description: Implement configuration and runtime changes that allow distinct external system connections for the same binding type, update endpoint resolution and lifecycle handling, preserve existing configuration behavior, and add focused unit tests.

activities.activity_name: HDFS HA custom module location support
activities.activity_description: Update custom module location resolution to honor Hadoop HA nameservice configuration, use the appropriate HA-aware client or proxy creation path, handle configuration errors, and add tests for HA and non-HA configurations.

Move the Cassandra module from the XD repository to the s-c-s repository, adapt package and build metadata, wire it into the target module conventions, preserve sink behavior, and add or port module-level tests.

Port the analytic-PMML module into the s-c-s repository, adapt dependencies and packaging, preserve processor semantics and configuration, and add or port tests covering representative PMML processing.
Add a REST endpoint or compatible extension to return whether a job is standalone or part of a composition, including DTOs, service-layer mapping, validation, serialization, and API tests.

Implement a REST endpoint that returns composition nodes and parent-child edges, define stable JSON semantics, handle standalone and nested cases, prevent duplicate or cyclic traversal issues, and add controller and integration tests.

Update the job list and related UI views to visually distinguish composed workflows from standalone jobs, consume the composition metadata, and display appropriate labels, icons, or layout treatment consistent with the existing UI.

activities.activity_name: Job detail navigation for composed and standalone jobs
activities.activity_description: Implement click-through behavior from either a standalone job or a composed-job entity to the correct job detail page, including route parameter handling, links from graph nodes, loading states, and error or missing-entity behavior.

activities.activity_name: Cross-feature automated testing and regression fixes
activities.activity_description: Add integration coverage across REST, job composition data, UI/API interactions, module packaging, binding scenarios, and HDFS configuration; run the existing regression suite and fix defects found during integration.

Document new binding configuration, HDFS HA requirements, migrated module coordinates and usage, composition endpoints, response examples, and UI behavior. Update relevant sample configuration and release notes.

Perform clean builds, dependency and packaging verification, manual end-to-end acceptance checks for all user stories, review changed interfaces for compatibility, and prepare the increment for merge or release.
